recipes.name: Baked Buffalo Wings
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup hot pepper sauce (such as Frank's RedHot®)

steps.text: Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil, and lightly grease with cooking spray.
Place flour, cayenne pepper, garlic powder, and salt into a resealable plastic bag, and shake to mix. Add chicken wings, seal the bag, and toss until well coated with the flour mixture.
Transfer wings to the prepared baking sheet and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
While the oven is preheating, whisk together melted butter and hot sauce in a small bowl.
Dip wings into butter mixture, and place back on the baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Flip wings and continue to cook until crispy on the outside and no longer pink in the center, about 25 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Buffalo Wings
raw_recipe.description: These spicy baked Buffalo wings are crispy without being fried, super easy to prep, and perfect for feeding a crowd! Great for parties or game watching!

video.description: You might be surprised to learn that you don't need a deep fryer to make the best chicken wings of your life. In this video, learn how to make baked buffalo wings that will surely satisfy the crowd at your next tailgate. They get their memorable crunch from a quick stay in the refrigerator before baking, and it makes these restaurant-worthy wings as crispy as it gets. Feel free to add more cayenne or hot sauce if you like them spicier!

review.reviewBody: Make sure your wings are dry before dredging in the flour, should help with them not be so soggy if that's the issue you are having. Also, this recipe is pretty easy to customize to your taste, you can add different sauces and herbs. You can bake these wings on a roasting pan if you want. I've been getting lazy and using parchment paper so that I don't have to use cooking spray, kind of messy, haha. Thanks for everyone's input, I'm so glad you like the recipe!

This recipe offers a good alternative way to make buffalo wings than the traditional deep-fried. It's easy and tastes great. It's good to make ahead for parties. If your wings didn't end up with crispy skin or came out soggy, it may have to do with the wings aren't dry enough. My suggestion is to dry your wings on a drainer after rising. Then pat dry (or even squeeze a little) with paper towel. If your wings are dry enough, they should coat nicely with the flour. Refrigerate without the plastic wrap can also help drying the wings. Do not soak your wings into the butter and hot sauce mixture for too long. If juice comes out during baking, drain it. This should make the crispy skin. I might also try making them in different favors such as lemon pepper or honey lime, etc.

Excellent! My suggestions to avoid soggy wings (1) Make sure to dry wings before flour dredge, (2) "Rest" wings uncovered in fridge for longer time (3) Line baking sheet or broiler pan with aluminum foil and place cooling rack or equivalent on lined pan, then bake wings on the rack. The grease will drip down into the pan and the wings will cook without soaking in the grease. This is an excellent alternative to fried wings, and being from the Buffalo area, I can say with confidence that these are comparable to those served in this area. Well done!

I have always baked my buffalo wings, but this is the first time I've drenched them in flour prior to baking them. I only added 3 tsp of cayenne pepper to the flour because 5 tsp seemed excessive. The wings were crispy and juicy on the inside. Definitely the best wings I've ever made. Thanks for sharing!

I made them before exactly as written and they were okay. After I adjusted the recipe, my son refuses to go back to the frozen Buffalo wings I used to buy! First off, I did NOT use foil, the wings stuck to it horribly the first time I made them. Instead, I used parchment paper. To the sauce, I added a dash of onion powder and garlic powder. I used only 1/3 c. of butter and 1/2 c. of hot sauce because the sauce was not hot enough for my guys. I did not dip the wings in the hot sauce mixture or put the wings in the fridge. I put them right in the oven. Saved time and they were just as crispy. I baked (40, but I didn't have to double the flour mixture) party wings (wings that were already cut in half) at 410F for 25 minutes one one side, and then flip for 25 another minutes and then broiled for 5 minutes. I took them out and then dumped them in the pot with the sauce and then tossed them until fully coated. Another time, I also cut up 2 large breasts. I used my amount of seasoning in the flour. Put the pieces on parchment paper and in a 400 degree oven for 20 minutes, flipped and put in for 20 more minutes. Amazing!

There was more than enough of the flour mixture in the bag so I made a few extra. It made about 30 wings total, which is half of the "party pack" from Costco. I placed them in 2 foil-line baking sheets and baked them in the oven before adding any of the sauce (they won't get soggy). Flip after 25 minutes. Take out after 20 more. To make the sauce I just mixed a stick of butter and the whole bottle of Frank's Red Hot (Xtra Hot) in a glass baking dish. Place wings in glass dish & turn to coat both sides. Put dish in oven 5 minutes. My husband says they're really good.

Really loved this recipe! Didn’t even finish the meal and my wife was already talking about making it again and different sauce options (did half buffalo half bbq for the first try). Like others, dried the wings before adding to the flour and let sit in the fridge for about an hour. Cooked on a wire rack on a baking sheet at 425* for about 45 min, spritzing them with cooking spray before putting them in the oven (and again when I flipped at 25 min). Once cooked through, dipped them in sauce and then broiled on low for 5 min. Came out crispy and delicious! This is definitely part of the rotation going forward!

This is a good recipe I use as a great baseline for me. Typically I will rinse the wings then pat them dry with paper towels (skipping the refridgeration). Then coat the wings adding extra Louisiana spice and black pepper on the wings. I have substituted the flour with a mix of half and half Almond and coconut flour for a keto friendly non gluten version. Then I place the wings on a oiled or coated cooling rack on top of my cookie tray and bake them so they don't sit in any juices. But sprayed the tops with a light coat of butter. Flipped after 20 minutes, spayed the flipped side with a light coat of butter. After they bake the last 25 minutes, I then brush them with the butter wing sauce and sometimes add my favorite BBQ sauce to the mixture as well. You can either serve immediately or put them back in the oven 5 minutes to set the sauce.

LOVED IT! I baked the wings @400 on middle shelf for almost 1 hr, after having dried them out with a clean towel and then coating with PLAIN flour. As said by a previous user: I highly recommend baking the chicken wings fully, THEN tossing them in the sauce, and putting them back in the oven on broil for 3-4 mins. Perfect. THAT TOTALLY WORKED FOR ME. THANKS FOR SHARING!

I changed this up bit. I used a baking sheet and coated it with olive oil. I coated the wings and laid them out after coating them and put them in the fridge for an hour. I preheated the over to 400. I cooked them for 30 minutes, I drained the grease, baked them another 25 minutes, flipped them over, baked them another 15 minutes and THEN rolled them in the butter and tapito sauce and then baked them another 10 minutes. I pulled a few suggestions from other bakers together to make it come out just so great.

I'm glad I read reviews before I made them. I made some modifications. I am not sure why there is butter in the recipe? You add it to the sauce and I think that would separate a little and be mushy. I dont know. I also let these rest with the flour mixture for about 6-7 hours and not just 1. I omitted the cayenne pepper but thats a personal preference. Its pretty potent and my husband's stomach cant tolerate too much. I also didnt dunk my wings in sauce. We dont prefer a ton of sauce and dont want them drowning. I used a pastry brush and brushed both sides really well. Turned out perfect. My wings were huge so I cooked for an hour turning halfway through and that was great timing. This is a decent recipe but needs to be tweaked to your personal preferences. I still dont understand the butter so I dont know if thats right. Probably why a lot of people complained of mushy wings. These were so tender inside and crispy outside. Yum.
IT WAS GREAT AS IS

I added some ground herbs like chives, oregano, thyme and more garlic powder. I did nor refrigerate the 1 hour so I added a little more flour to the mix. The chicken wings were previously frozen and still Ice cold. I used the Mike's red hot sauce mixed with butter as a dipping sauce, one cup Mike's red hot sauce and 1 cup unsalted butter, melted and whisked into the hot sauce.
My husband is very picky! He loves this recipe!

I used this recipe with whole chicken wings and found that the cook time and temperature still worked perfectly. I doubled the garlic powder but otherwise made it as written and these were a hit at the Super Bowl party! I appreciate that they aren't soggy and the sauce stays on well.
All I did was add teriyaki sauce c e to the hot sauce and butter. Best juicy wings I've had in a long time
Very easy and super yummy

I follow recipe except I bake wings without the sauce as I’ve had varied results doing that. I just toss the wings into the sauce once baked. A little more messy to eat but still delicious. I use a rack over parchment paper for easy clean up and more even baking
I love this recipe. I alternated regular flour with almond flour.
Really good, not greasy. Use 1 teaspoon of cayenne pepper, 1/4 cup of butter, 3/4 cup of hot sauce. Air fry 20 min at 400○.
